title: Add a lightweight, server-side-filtered search for cross-repo task lookup
description:
git-task-web's global search box (top bar — matches project name + task display_id/title across every registered repo) currently reuses `ls --all --format json`, which returns the FULL task payload (description, comments, links, labels, etc.) for every task in every repo, just so the web client can filter by a short substring client-side.

That's fine at small scale — it's still a single CLI spawn, not one per repo — but it doesn't scale well: as repo/task/comment volume grows, the payload the client fetches and parses for a quick-jump search grows right along with it, even though search only ever needs a handful of fields.

Requested: a lightweight, server-side-filtered listing — e.g. `git task search <query>` or `git task ls --all --search <text>` — that matches against id/display_id/title (and ideally description/labels, for real full-text search) and returns a minimal projection (id, display_id, title, kind, status, repo/project) instead of the full task shape.

Not urgent — id/title matching already works fine today via `ls --all` at current scale. This is a forward-looking ask so the web client isn't stuck shipping full task payloads over HTTP just to power a search box, and so description/comment full-text search becomes feasible without that cost.

Filed from git-task-web after adding its global search box.
